description:
Kmeng Steav also known as Bek Sloy is a youth subculture in Cambodia that was prevalent in the early 2010s, most likely characterized by riding customized motorbikes, flashy basic street, richy-counterfeit fashion, and energetic group dancing to electronic/techno music during events like Khmer New Year. Similar to regional substyles such as the Philippines' Jejemon , China's Shamate or Thailand's " Dek Waen " which represents an rebellious, expressive urban youth identity.

Kmeng steav's ( ក្មេងស្ទាវ ) slang phrase from Cambodia translates to "street-style bad boy," "rebellious youth," or "young gangster" which describes someone young who acts wild, tough, or cool in a street-smart way. This subculture also features individuals trying to be cute but in a "gangster" way which can include dramatic dance / hand postures.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Self-Expression, Conformity, Party-Like Attitude
